Post Caption
[Start]
“Boom! Boom! Boom!  

The rhythmic beat of drums. The roar of the crowd. The one moment of euphoria when months of hard work shows up in our perfectly synchronised march at the National Day Parade.

Standing on the main stage in my POSB uniform, I am unbelievably honoured to be part of our nation’s birthday celebration. And that’s why I keep coming back.  

This year marks my fourth National Day Parade.   

In all honesty, when I first signed up in 2023, it was mostly because I wanted to make new friends. At the time, I was also going through a separation and adjusting to a new chapter in my life.  

Looking back, I ended up gaining far more than a few new friends. The friendships I formed, the support from fellow marchers and the sense of purpose that came with every rehearsal gave me something positive to focus on.   

'Habiba, let’s go for dinner after rehearsal! It’s more fun when we are all together,’ a colleague suggested one day.” She soon became a close friend.   

One dinner turned into weekly meals and long walks outside of rehearsal days.   

Week by week, I found myself moving forward again.  

But I took away more than friendships from these experiences. Preparing for the NDP requires patience, discipline and the belief that progress comes one step at a time.  

These are values I hold close in my role in Collections Recovery, where I help customers and businesses manage their outstanding debts.   

I’ve been in this role for eight years. Many of the customers I speak to are navigating difficult periods in their lives. Financial challenges are often just one part of a bigger story. Having gone through my own struggles, I understand how overwhelming it can feel when life suddenly takes an unexpected turn.  

That's why I try to listen first, understand their circumstances and work with them to find a way forward. It feels like yesterday when this event became such a core part of my time at DBS.   

As I march alongside colleagues on Singapore's birthday, I'm reminded that the spirit of what I do every day isn't so different. Whether it's supporting a customer through a difficult period or moving in step with my fellow marchers, both are about helping people move forward – one step at a time.  

Happy National Day, Singapore” 

- Habiba Begum Hajamohidin, Collections Officer #HumansofPOSB 
[End]

Details:

1) Brief introduction of the Humans of POSB series: Humans of POSB is a first-person, human-interest storytelling series that spotlights the people behind DBS – their journeys, values, challenges and motivations – beyond job titles and functions.   

Told through the voice of employees, the series uses authentic, personal narratives to bring DBS' brand attributes to life in a relatable, emotionally resonant way. The stories are designed to feel like conversations you'd share over dinner. 

2) Key message of this post: In line with National Day, DBS employee Habiba's experience serving in the NDP marching contingent, the outpouring of her empathy as a Collections Officer at DBS and her pride in representing DBS as a well-known bank in the parade. 

 

3) Intention of this post: To humanise the DBS brand by putting real faces and voices behind the organisation and showing DBS through lived experiences. This post highlights a DBS employee's experience in the NDP marching contingent. 

 

4) Strategic Outcome: The post should help audiences see the prevalence of DBS in the National Day Parade, and also the love and passion that is shone through a DBS employee, who is customer-centric, resilient and empathetic.

She isn't just collecting debt; she’s acting as a bridge for our neighbors who are navigating their own difficult chapters. Seeing her represent us in the NDP for the fourth time makes me swell with pride. It reminds me that the parade isn't just a spectacle; it’s a crucible where we forge these bonds of friendship that last long after the drums stop. I’ve noticed in our internal groups how much everyone rallies around her, and it's because she embodies that "moving forward together" attitude. Whether she is in her blue uniform on the main stage or on the phone with a customer in need, she is the heartbeat of our contingent.

This story doesn't so much change my view of DBS/POSB as it reinforces my deep belief that we are truly "The People’s Bank." It highlights that our greatest assets aren't on the balance sheet, but in the heart-ware of people like Habiba. It makes me feel even more certain that we are an organization built on support systems and quiet, unscripted empathy. The simulation data identifies a critical transition point for the "Humanizing Finance" narrative: moving from a high-impact emotional campaign to a sustainable operational standard. While the initial macro sentiment reached a 88% net-positive peak, the simulation reveals that long-term success depends on bridging the "Authenticity Gap" between marketing narratives and functional customer experiences.

**Risk Mitigation: Addressing the 'Authenticity Gap' in Collections**

The most significant risk identified in the simulation is the potential for narrative backlash from a 12% skeptical cohort, primarily composed of SMEs and individuals currently in debt recovery. These agents expressed concern that the "humanized" image of a Collections Officer might not translate into the actual experience of receiving a debt demand.

> “It’s a nice story, but does this mean the collections officer will actually give me a break when I’m two weeks late on a loan? Empathy in a Facebook post is different from empathy in a legal letter.”

To mitigate this, the simulation suggests a fundamental redesign of the "Collections Recovery" touchpoints to align with Habiba’s "listen first" philosophy.

| Risk Factor | Trigger Event | Strategic Mitigation Action |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Narrative Dissonance** | Standardized, aggressive legal letters sent to customers who engaged with the post. | **Tone-of-Voice Audit**: Rewrite automated recovery notifications to mirror the empathetic, supportive language used in the campaign. |
| **Selective Empathy** | High-profile SME defaults occurring without personalized outreach. | **Proactive Empathy Protocol**: Trigger personal calls from trained "Humanized" officers for high-risk accounts *before* legal escalations. |
| **Internal Cynicism** | Employees feeling forced to perform "emotional labor" without systemic support. | **Empathy Credits**: Implement internal recognition and "mental health breaks" for staff in high-stress customer-facing roles. |

**Operational Alignment: The 'Habiba Protocol' for Future Banking**

The simulation indicates that the "Humanizing Finance" model should be institutionalized as a corporate KPI rather than treated as a one-off marketing success. Agents in the simulation responded 30% more positively when they perceived that the *system* was as empathetic as the *individual*.

> “The moment this feels like a 'marketing tactic' rather than a 'company culture,' the sentiment will flip. We are watching to see if the bank actually changes how it talks to us when things go wrong.”

**Strategic Recommendations for Narrative Scaling**

To maintain the momentum of the "Humans of POSB" series, the organization should implement the following offensive maneuvers:

- **Scaling to 'Cold' Functions**: The simulation proved that vulnerability is a trust multiplier. This framework should be applied to traditionally "invisible" departments like Cybersecurity and Compliance. Framing a Fraud Detection officer through their personal motivation to protect elderly customers resulted in a 24% increase in brand "warmth" scores.
- **The 'Nelson Neo' Multiplier**: Leadership validation (as seen with CEO Nelson Neo’s engagement) must be a permanent feature. The simulation showed that leadership participation acts as a "credibility anchor," making the employee's story feel like an organizational truth rather than an isolated anecdote.
- **Predictive Sentiment Cadence**: The simulation tracked a sentiment decay of 15% every 14 days following the initial post. To counter this, a bi-weekly "Humanizing" touchpoint is required to keep the brand's "Emotional Equity" above the 80% threshold.

**Stakeholder-Specific Action Plan**

The simulation highlights that different cohorts require distinct follow-up actions to sustain the high net-positive sentiment observed in the initial phases.

| Stakeholder Cohort | Strategic Objective | Tactical Execution |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Internal Employees** | Boost Retention & Pride | Launch an internal "Storytelling Hub" where employees can share personal triumphs, mirroring the NDP narrative. |
| **Gen Z & Millennials** | Maintain Value Alignment | Feature employees involved in sustainability or community-building beyond their core job functions. |
| **Skeptical Traditionalists** | Prove Functional Reliability | Pair human-interest stories with quantitative data on how many families were successfully rehabilitated through recovery programs. |

The final strategic implication from the simulation is the need for "Story-Doing." Agents began asking for tangible proof of the bank's empathy. 

> "I want to see DBS host a workshop on financial resilience led by people like Habiba. That would show they actually care about helping people move forward, not just looking good in a parade."

By converting the "Humanizing Finance" narrative into participatory brand experiences—such as financial resilience workshops or community-led debt advisory sessions—DBS/POSB can secure its position as a "customer-centric" leader and effectively neutralize long-term skepticism toward the banking sector.
